# Hari Meyyappan

> AI Practice Lead at qBotica (since 2023). Builds AI agents for production: voice agents, document extraction, banking and recruiting agents. Before that, 3 years at Amazon (Alexa Shopping routing, AWS). MS CS, Arizona State; B.Tech, NIT Trichy. Writes notes on building AI agents, personal apps, and tools for thought.

- Home: https://hmeyy.com/
- Zettelkasten (short notes): https://hmeyy.com/zettelkasten/
- Quotes: https://hmeyy.com/quotes/
- Archive of all writing: https://hmeyy.com/archive.html
- Email: hari.m.subbiah@gmail.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/harimeyy/
- GitHub: https://github.com/jagwarrx
- Feed: https://hmeyy.com/feed.xml

## Writing

- [Active Learning Is the Only Learning](https://hmeyy.com/essays/active-learning.html): Reading is not learning. Reading is familiarizing. Thinking, reasoning and recalling are learning.
- [Modelling ADHD Attention as a Stack](https://hmeyy.com/essays/adhd-attention-stack.html): ADHD attention works like a stack: the last thing in is the first thing out, and only the top is top of mind. Importance doesn’t move an item up; only being new does. So build the priority queue outside, and let the head be a stack.
- [What Difference Does ADHD Medication Make?](https://hmeyy.com/essays/adhd-medication.html): It turns the noise down. It doesn't choose what to focus on, and it doesn't pick itself up from the pharmacy. A practical answer, not medical advice.
- [The ADHD Monkey Wrench: Diffused Attention](https://hmeyy.com/essays/adhd-monkey-wrench.html): Diffused attention affects sustained attention. I can focus only when something is novel or high stakes, so important things wait until they seem dangerous and new things get done at once. The fix is to borrow the stakes early, on purpose.
- [The Language of an ADHD System](https://hmeyy.com/essays/adhd-system-language.html): What the external system should say to an ADHD brain, and how, so the brain can take it in and act. Seven messages: what now, how much, by when, done so far, not now, stop, and you drifted. Each one short, seen, at the right moment, and in the same place every day.
- [The ADHD Version of the Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/adhd-version-of-the-need.html): The need for meaning under uncertainty is the same in ADHD, but its time horizon isn't: the far future pulls less and the next ten minutes pull more. How that works, why the traits survive, and what follows.
- [Your agent will say it sent the email](https://hmeyy.com/essays/agent-said-it-sent-the-email.html): What it takes to let an AI agent act on real systems: the rules I ended up writing into every agent that can change a record.
- [Answers That Compound](https://hmeyy.com/essays/answers-that-compound.html): Why buying the answer to the need wins in the moment, and why it loses over time: made answers compound up, bought ones compound down, and the self-made answer has to be built cold for a need that fires hot.
- [Dealing with Anxiety When You Have ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/anxiety-and-adhd.html): About half of adults with ADHD have had an anxiety disorder, and much of it grows out of the traits. Where it comes from, how to calm it in the moment, and how to make the alarm go off less.
- [The Art of Defense](https://hmeyy.com/essays/art-of-defense.html): Defending against manipulation, once your position is secure: learn the tactics in advance, rely on process, name the tactic, stay trusting. Most of it is done beforehand, not in the moment, and it is the same defense as against bullshit.
- [Artificial Intelligence: Where to dig](https://hmeyy.com/essays/artificial-intelligence-where-to-dig.html): Improve features, create features, create products. The easier problems first.
- [Ask a Better Question](https://hmeyy.com/essays/ask-a-better-question.html): Before I build a tool, I stop and ask what I'm trying to achieve and whether there's an easier, quicker or better way. Often that way is to run the thing through a prompt first.
- [Avoid, Detect, Remove Bullshit with ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/avoid-detect-remove-bullshit.html): Bullshit in claims and in systems both come from the need for meaning. ADHD can’t keep up vigilance, so the defense has to be fast, written down, run at a calm time, and removal has to happen by default.
- [Balance Is the Ground, Not the Goal](https://hmeyy.com/essays/balance-is-the-ground.html): Devout societies aren’t reliably peaceful; practiced ones are more often. The body wants rhythm, not a fixed point. And most traditions treat balance as the path to the highest things, not the highest thing.
- [Is Behavior the Language of Life?](https://hmeyy.com/essays/behavior-is-a-language.html): Behavior communicates something. Words, behaviors and deeds are all saying something about you, and deeds say it loudest. Gandhi called his life a set of experiments with truth. This is probably what is meant by character.
- [Is There a Best Possible Study Plan for a Subject?](https://hmeyy.com/essays/best-study-plan.html): No single one, but there is a best plan for a given goal and person, and good plans share a structure: an end test, a map, concepts with cases, retrieval, tacit practice and a changing surface.
- [The Block Method](https://hmeyy.com/essays/block-method.html): David Cain's method for the productivity-challenged: 25 minutes, uninterrupted, aimed at finishing a task, tallied on a sticky note. Any goal is a number of Blocks. And it climbs the Wall of Awful, because a Block never asks for the whole task, only for the next 25 minutes.
- [Bottom-Up Programming for Enlightenment](https://hmeyy.com/essays/bottom-up-enlightenment.html): Paul Graham said to build the language up toward the program. Shinzen Young did that for the mind: six small words for experience, and practices short enough to fit in a sentence.
- [Buddhism Through the Lens of the Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/buddhism-and-the-need.html): Pleasure is designed not to last, for the same reason uncertainty hurts: the brain is a prediction machine. Buddhism named both sides, craving and aversion, and is the only tradition that treats the need itself as the problem.
- [Change the Environment to Change the Actions](https://hmeyy.com/essays/change-the-environment.html): Change the environment and the situation, which changes the constraints, which changes the actions. The levers work on different time scales: minutes, days, months, years.
- [Cheap Substitutes for Real Needs](https://hmeyy.com/essays/cheap-substitutes.html): A supernormal stimulus is a beer bottle a beetle mistakes for a mate. Status, the feed and flattering AI imitate competence, presence and relatedness: reward now, wanting without liking, signal without substance, no resistance. Use substitutes for rest, not as the main meal.
- [Choosing a Task](https://hmeyy.com/essays/choosing-a-task.html): The gap between the best task and the third-best is usually smaller than the time spent agonizing over it. Choose fast: before I need to, with one fixed tiebreaker, from a menu of three, in sixty seconds, two at a time.
- [Coach Wooden](https://hmeyy.com/essays/coach-wooden.html): John Wooden's seven rules for living, and why they still hold.
- [Compounding in the Real World](https://hmeyy.com/essays/compounding-real-world.html): On paper compounding is a smooth curve. In a life it’s messy and mostly invisible: it comes late, in lumps, after a lag, through other people, into limits and sometimes in reverse, with no statement to show the stock. Track the inputs, judge it in years, and don’t interrupt it.
- [Constraints Drive Actions](https://hmeyy.com/essays/constraints-drive-actions.html): What you do is mostly decided by the limits you work inside. Treat your traits as constraints to design around, not failings to fix with effort.
- [Control, and Letting the World Play Out](https://hmeyy.com/essays/control-and-letting-go.html): Too little control is helplessness; too much makes you fragile. The old split between what is in your power and what is not, observation to tell them apart, and slack to leave room when the world moves.
- [Culture, Entertainment and the Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/culture-entertainment-need.html): We pay not to know what comes next. Entertainment sells safe uncertainty with an ending guaranteed, culture answers it for everyone at once, the feed removes the ending, and improv answers it differently.
- [Design the Data and the Features Together](https://hmeyy.com/essays/design-together.html): Designing the data is designing what the app can do. Like a language and a program in Lisp, data and features should be designed together, with the interface as a surface on top.
- [Direction, Time, Energy](https://hmeyy.com/essays/direction-time-energy.html): Seven layers, from what it’s all for down to the fuel. Direction at the top, time in the middle, energy at the bottom. If any one of them is zero, the whole result is zero.
- [Aim to Be Directionally Correct](https://hmeyy.com/essays/directionally-correct.html): Precision is expensive. Direction is what compounds.
- [Arrange Things So You Don’t Need to Know](https://hmeyy.com/essays/dont-need-to-know.html): Taleb’s answer to the need: you can’t know what comes next, so arrange things so you don’t need to. Fragile, robust and antifragile; how smoothing makes us fragile; options, the barbell, via negativa, Lindy and small doses of stress.
- [If You Don’t See It, It Doesn’t Exist](https://hmeyy.com/essays/dont-see-it.html): If I don't see it, it doesn't exist: tasks buried in a project, a deadline next week, a tool I don't open, options spread across places. It's also a lever. Put in view what should stay alive, hide what should go away, and decide what's in view on purpose.
- [Dynamic Equilibrium](https://hmeyy.com/essays/dynamic-equilibrium.html): Balance that looks still but is two flows matched, like a reaction at equilibrium or a body holding its temperature. Control and letting go work this way, and so do sellers and buyers: no one holds the point, both sides keep it.
- [I built my personal system eighteen times](https://hmeyy.com/essays/eighteen-systems.html): Eighteen attempts in a year at a system to run my life. The median lasted four days. What survived had no schema at all.
- [Every Rep Makes the Next One Easier](https://hmeyy.com/essays/every-rep.html): Superstitions are self-perpetuating, so it’s better to nip them in the bud. Same with bad habits, mental and behavioral: every rep makes the next one easier. Knowing a belief is wrong doesn’t change the behavior; new experience does.
- [Free of Tools](https://hmeyy.com/essays/free-of-tools.html): Not the tool with all the features, but the freedom to be free of tools: plain text, picked up anywhere, anytime. For ADHD, the ritual gets done because it’s simple.
- [Free Up the Higher Mind](https://hmeyy.com/essays/free-up-the-higher-mind.html): Every person has some divinity and some badness, at different levels at different times. Observe how they move you, keep a healthy balance, and automate the routine with habits, rituals and rules so the higher mind has room.
- [Good Strategy, Bad Strategy](https://hmeyy.com/essays/good-strategy-bad-strategy.html): Rumelt’s kernel: a diagnosis, a guiding policy, coherent actions. Bad strategy skips the problem and the choice. Pick the crux, the challenge that is critical and solvable, and use strategy only where something important is blocked and unclear.
- [Habits That Sustain](https://hmeyy.com/essays/habits-that-sustain.html): The pyramid of habits. At the base: exercise, water, medication. On the next level: hygiene, nutrition, sleep, planning. Each level holds up the one above. On a bad day the base is the whole goal, and when the week falls apart, repair from the bottom.
- [Happiness Can Be Designed, Partly](https://hmeyy.com/essays/happiness-can-be-designed.html): A sense of control is called locus of control. Newport’s three needs, and three things that predict a good day: connection, presence and progress. You can design the conditions for happiness, not the feeling.
- [How Many Responses You Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/how-many-responses.html): If you fix the response instead of the forecast, how many responses do you need? Ashby’s law says enough to match the world, but three escape routes leave about five, plus one default.
- [How to Win Hackathons](https://hmeyy.com/essays/how-to-win-hackathons.html): A guide to winning hackathons: making marginal gains in ideation, team formation, prototyping and presentation.
- [Improvised Productivity](https://hmeyy.com/essays/improvised-productivity.html): Start a timer, then figure it out. Novelty plays a key role, and a timer, money and people each add a sense of stakes. Three ways it fails, four small fixes, and one honest test.
- [Peter Kaufman on Interdisciplinary Thinking](https://hmeyy.com/essays/interdisciplinary-thinking.html): Notes on the talk that made multidisciplinary thinking click.
- [Is the Need the Core Need?](https://hmeyy.com/essays/is-the-need-the-core-need.html): A hard look at the frame behind these essays. As the first human need, it holds up; as the only one, it doesn’t. Belonging looks just as basic, we seek surprise as well as certainty, and a frame that explains everything needs testing.
- [Know How You’ll Meet It](https://hmeyy.com/essays/know-how-youll-meet-it.html): You can’t know what comes next, but you can know how you’ll meet it. That’s a different answer to the need: fix the response, not the forecast. The Stoics, the Gita, armies, pilots and improv all found it.
- [The Language ADHD Speaks](https://hmeyy.com/essays/language-adhd-speaks.html): ADHD processes a certain kind of language: now, seen, felt, concrete and short. It barely hears importance, the future, abstractions or should. So managing ADHD is mostly translation: the plan is written in importance, and the day has to run in now.
- [The Language of Systems](https://hmeyy.com/essays/language-of-systems.html): Every system has a language, and learning a system is mostly discovering its words and learning them. Language is a tool, maybe the first one: in the brain, making tools and making sentences share ground. Once I have the word, I can see the thing.
- [Layers of Operations](https://hmeyy.com/essays/layers-of-operations.html): Plan, capture, choose, work, log. A personal system designed like a software system: requirements, entities, flow, layers, then the tools. A tool can be swapped; a layer can't be skipped.
- [The Structural Lens and the Stack](https://hmeyy.com/essays/lens-and-stack.html): The stack of effectiveness is the anatomy of a life: what the parts are and which serves which. The structural lens is the physiology of a choice: how a decision moves from frame to outcome and back. Each shows what the other can't see.
- [Lessons In Crypto Markets](https://hmeyy.com/essays/lessons-in-crypto-markets.html): What a year of trading taught me about risk, patience and myself.
- [How to Let the Rest Play Out](https://hmeyy.com/essays/let-the-rest-play-out.html): Letting the rest play out is letting go: full effort on your part, an open hand on the result. In the world but not of it; name the line, count your part as done, act and release, review at the right scale, leave slack.
- [Levels of Leverage: Where to Intervene](https://hmeyy.com/essays/levels-of-leverage.html): Donella Meadows ranked twelve places to intervene in a system. Mapped onto the stack of effectiveness: direction holds the most leverage, plans the least, and the loops between layers are where most fixes live. Diagnose bottom-up, intervene top-down.
- [The Levers on How You Respond](https://hmeyy.com/essays/levers-on-response.html): Eight levers decide how you respond, in the order they act: situation, cues, state and prepared responses before; the gap, attention and meaning during; review after. The earlier the lever, the better it works.
- [Life, Quarter, Week, Day](https://hmeyy.com/essays/life-quarter-week-day.html): Connection, presence and progress are descriptive principles; rewrite them as A over B. Each scale of a life needs its own guidance: principles for a life, strategy for a quarter, rhythm for a week, presence for a day.
- [A List of Lists, One Item at a Time](https://hmeyy.com/essays/list-of-lists.html): My tradeoff: organize items in a list of lists, but look at them one at a time. Organizing wants to see everything. Doing, with an ADHD mind, wants to see one thing.
- [Lists of Book Lists](https://hmeyy.com/essays/lists-of-book-lists.html): The reading lists I go back to when choosing what to read next.
- [Log the Block, Don’t Start It](https://hmeyy.com/essays/log-the-block.html): One button to log, with two types: blocks and habits. The block starts on a sticky note; the app only logs it once it's done.
- [Manage Commitments, Not Tasks](https://hmeyy.com/essays/manage-commitments.html): For ADHD, change the question from how to be productive to what you’ve promised, to whom, and whether you can keep it. The root causes of broken commitments, and how to promise differently, free of tools.
- [The Market for the Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/market-for-the-need.html): The need never changes, but the market for it does: four dials, a history from the band to the feed, why religion is now sold in pieces, and what a mass audience is.
- [Meaning Makes Pain Bearable](https://hmeyy.com/essays/meaning-makes-pain-bearable.html): Meaning turns pain into a cost paid for something. Viktor Frankl, the soldiers at Anzio and modern pain science, why it works on resistance and on the need, and where it stops being true.
- [Mechanics of a System](https://hmeyy.com/essays/mechanics-of-a-system.html): The state machine is one of six pictures that hold at every scale. The others are the function, the log, the graph, the queue and the loop. What each one answers, the six questions to ask of any system, and what they leave to cost, people and uncertainty.
- [Meeting the Need with ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/meeting-the-need-adhd.html): Four parts of the need, four fixes. Not knowing what to do: decide the night before. Faint time: make it visible. Waiting hurts: bring the reward close. Can’t keep a ritual going: automate it.
- [Meeting the Need Yourself](https://hmeyy.com/essays/meeting-the-need-yourself.html): How much of the need can you meet without buying it? Most of the core: the boundary, meaning in the act, your own experience library, surprise as material, adapting, putting it outside. Not community, and not death.
- [The Minimum System for ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/minimum-system-adhd.html): Two lists. One with everything. One with what is important now, three items at most.
- [Minimum Viable Tool](https://hmeyy.com/essays/minimum-viable-tool.html): The smallest kit that runs my days: do a block and log it against a project, count blocks against a target, track habits, move projects on a kanban board, and keep everything else on sticky notes and a scratchpad with a timer. The app part is one small page called Blocks.
- [Modelling State Machines](https://hmeyy.com/essays/modelling-state-machines.html): Most of a syllabus for software systems is one idea: state plus rules, and machines sending messages. One pattern, many substrates, each with its own physics; where the lens stops working; and why AI systems feel different.
- [The Automated Morning Brief](https://hmeyy.com/essays/morning-brief.html): One short message every morning, without my asking: the three things for today, the first step, and the fixed times. Why that would help an ADHD brain.
- [The Nation as Religion](https://hmeyy.com/essays/nation-as-religion.html): Run the nation-state through the five questions of The Bundle and it passes almost every test of a religion. It fails two, power and exit, and that makes its fine print the heaviest.
- [What I Need, Not What I Can](https://hmeyy.com/essays/need-not-can.html): Obsidian, or any tool like it, is too flexible. Trying to do everything with it, you don’t do what you need. So start with the few jobs you need it for.
- [Negotiation Needs Structure and Empathy](https://hmeyy.com/essays/negotiation-structure-empathy.html): Getting to Yes gives the structure: interests, alternatives, fair standards. Never Split the Difference gives the skills: mirroring, labeling, calibrated questions. Use the empathy tools always, the bargaining tactics only in one-off deals.
- [Build the Network Before You Need It](https://hmeyy.com/essays/network-before-you-need-it.html): Never Eat Alone is what comes before any negotiation: relationships that give you options and allies. Weak ties pay off, otherish givers rise, and a network built early is your alternative at the table.
- [Not Tools, but Automation](https://hmeyy.com/essays/not-tools-but-automation.html): For managing attention, a tool is the wrong shape: it waits for me to remember it. Automation runs on the days I forget.
- [The Unreasonable Effectiveness of a Number](https://hmeyy.com/essays/number-on-a-task.html): Review 10 cards. Five blocks on the essay. A number on a task, as long as it isn't time, gives it an end, a size and a score I can watch go up. It works far better than it should.
- [Observation Is a Tool](https://hmeyy.com/essays/observation-is-a-tool.html): You shape your tools, then your tools shape you. Observation, used often, becomes a tool, a faculty of attention. Everyone has access to the higher mind; they just need to train their observation on it.
- [Ode to Systems Thinking](https://hmeyy.com/essays/ode-to-systems-thinking.html): Consumers, creators and investors, and what it means to see the whole.
- [See Everything Together in One Place](https://hmeyy.com/essays/one-board.html): To make a decision, I need to see everything together on one master board. Out of sight is out of existence, so with things spread out, every choice comes with doubt about what I'm missing. One board closes the set. Decide on the board, work from the short list.
- [One Thing at a Time](https://hmeyy.com/essays/one-thing-at-a-time.html): A constraint worth adding: do one thing at a time, picked from a short menu, and don't drop it once it's started. The start is where neurospicy minds get tripped.
- [Suffering = Pain × Resistance](https://hmeyy.com/essays/pain-times-resistance.html): Shinzen Young’s formula, and what it would mean for resistance to go to zero: not zero pain, numbness or resignation, but full contact with no fight. The need to know what comes next is the second arrow.
- [Understand Power as Defense, Lean Towards Mastery](https://hmeyy.com/essays/power-as-defense.html): The 48 Laws of Power teaches the serpent, but it assumes royal courts, a zero-sum game. Careers are repeated games where reputation compounds. Read it as defense, to guard your autonomy, and lean towards mastery, the competence you can trade for the rest.
- [Power Is a Means](https://hmeyy.com/essays/power-is-a-means.html): Power is the currency under most of life’s games, so everyone needs some, and that is why it makes a bad goal. Where it sits among Smoley’s seven games, and why the principle to write down is a definition of enough.
- [Principles Are Guiding Policy for a Life](https://hmeyy.com/essays/principles-are-guiding-policy.html): Rumelt’s kernel of strategy, applied to a life: a diagnosis, a guiding policy and coherent actions. Values are the bedrock, principles the stake, policies the rope; tradeoffs decided ahead of time, and what to check when they stop working.
- [Principles, Experiments & Serendipity](https://hmeyy.com/essays/principles-experiments-serendipity.html): Turning 23. Lessons, professional and personal, and what comes next.
- [Projecting, Masking and ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/projecting-and-masking.html): What we project is a forecast of ourselves. ADHD makes that forecast hard to keep, masking holds it up with a private scramble, and what helps is paying for it in structure instead of effort.
- [Projects and Objectives](https://hmeyy.com/essays/projects-objectives.html): Objectives are concrete goals, like getting a new job. Projects are work with a finish line that moves them. Tasks, blocks and habits feed both. Above objectives is a want that is fuzzy and changes. The model has to be useful, not exact.
- [Ideas on Querying Dense Knowledge Bases](https://hmeyy.com/essays/querying-dense-knowledge-bases.html): A dense graph of hand-made notes breaks a plain retrieval agent three ways: priority, links and noise. One agent with three tools (lookup, sensemaking, discovery), lenses written as steps, and why a lens has to sit in the instructions, not the data.
- [Reason, Resonance & the Future](https://hmeyy.com/essays/reason-resonance-future.html): The future is created, not predicted. On meaning and what to build.
- [Religion as a Collective of the Higher Self](https://hmeyy.com/essays/religion-higher-self.html): Religion at its best is the higher mind of many people, organized. It gets captured two ways: by power, as weaponized religion, and by money, as commercial spirituality. Goodwill with discernment, and living from the Self.
- [Removing Bullshit](https://hmeyy.com/essays/removing-bullshit.html): Most of designing a system is taking things out: fields, features and rules that cost something every day and change nothing about what you do.
- [Scratch Notes, Permanent Notes and Artifacts](https://hmeyy.com/essays/scratch-notes.html): Scratch notes are the blocks layer: on paper or in Antinote. Project notes hold what's needed to reach an objective, like mindmaps in Heptabase or Excalidraw. Artifacts are cleaned up project notes I can reuse later. Permanent notes keep decisions and lists. A reminder goes on the timeline.
- [Secure Your Position First](https://hmeyy.com/essays/secure-your-position.html): The first move in defending against power plays: put yourself beyond defeat, then wait. Savings, skills, relationships and options are the safe end of the barbell, and it is hard to pressure someone who can walk away.
- [The Serpent and the Dove](https://hmeyy.com/essays/serpent-and-dove.html): Wise as serpents, harmless as doves: understanding the game fully while not playing dirty. The serpent sees danger and power games; the dove is unmixed, with clean motives. Each fails without the other.
- [Signal or Feature](https://hmeyy.com/essays/signal-or-feature.html): Every tradition sees that nothing satisfies for long. Is the restlessness a signal of something real we lack, or a feature of how the mind is built? Both fit the evidence, and both agree that nothing you can buy will be enough.
- [Learning with the Socratic Method](https://hmeyy.com/essays/socratic-learning.html): The best use of an LLM: not answers, but a tutor that asks one question at a time, aimed at the joints of my reasoning, so the shallow spots surface and get fixed.
- [The Spine and the Surface](https://hmeyy.com/essays/spine-and-surface.html): Why I kept losing things when I switched to-do apps, and the fix: keep a small, permanent spine and make everything around it disposable.
- [Spruced Up Planka](https://hmeyy.com/essays/spruced-up-planka.html): Planka is a free, open kanban board. Its calendar and timeline are paid. I kept its look and built what I needed on top: time on a calendar, swimlanes by date, focus blocks with targets, templates and typed fields. The full list of changes to the Community edition.
- [When It’s Not Working, Start](https://hmeyy.com/essays/start-when-stuck.html): Usually, when something is not working, I just need to start. Most failures I notice are things that never ran. Make the start tiny, name the first physical action, and start before I feel ready. Start first, fix second.
- [The Structural Lens](https://hmeyy.com/essays/structural-lens.html): The tool for the diagnosis stage of a strategy. When the same bad result keeps coming back, look for the cause in the structure, not the person: categories, constraints and defaults decide which questions you can ask, and everything after.
- [Suspiciously Neat](https://hmeyy.com/essays/suspiciously-neat.html): The stack, the lens and the OSI model are all vertical, and life may be more like a web. But the neatness isn’t a mistake: it’s legibility, the thing that makes a framework usable. Use the neat frame to act, and look for the loops when you review.
- [Tasks, Blocks and Habits](https://hmeyy.com/essays/tasks-blocks-habits.html): Tasks are units of commitment, blocks are time-bound units of effort, and habits are automated decisions. A task is a container: it holds a promise and the blocks it takes. Blocks are how I pay. Habits are the decisions I stop making.
- [How to Build and Test the Best Study Plan](https://hmeyy.com/essays/test-study-plan.html): Model memory as chunks with states, model each format by the state change it is good at, treat the plan as a schedule, and test it by splitting the subject, not the learner.
- [The Chupacabra](https://hmeyy.com/essays/the-chupacabra.html): A short story.
- [The Need Is Built In](https://hmeyy.com/essays/the-need-is-built-in.html): Why the need for meaning under uncertainty is so strong: how it works in the brain, why evolution built it, and what follows. The need is built in; sellers don't create it, they sell into it.
- [The Other: Trust the System, Not the Brain](https://hmeyy.com/essays/the-other.html): Why an ADHD brain needs something outside itself: a system, a person, a place. The inner voice that says not now, do this is weak, so the other has to come from outside. In the moment, the system outranks the brain.
- [Own the list, rent the app](https://hmeyy.com/essays/the-same-list.html): Any data structure can be a list, so every task manager can hold what any other can. What differs is the surface. Keep the data in one plain format and change the surface instead.
- [Three Layers of Dysregulation](https://hmeyy.com/essays/three-layers-of-dysregulation.html): Jenna Free's frame: a lot of my ADHD struggle is a nervous system stuck in fight-or-flight. Work on it in three layers, in order: calm the body, check the thoughts, then change the behavior.
- [Traditional To-Do Lists Don't Work for ADHD Brains](https://hmeyy.com/essays/todo-lists-adhd.html): Traditional to-do lists don't work for ADHD brains. We need focus and structure, not endless tasks.
- [Think in Trees, Do in Lists](https://hmeyy.com/essays/trees-and-lists.html): My ADHD brain thinks like a mind map, in trees, not in a line like a list. That's good for thinking and bad for doing. So I split them: think in mind maps, then force the doing into a list, one item after another.
- [The Unusual Effectiveness of Visual Language for ADHD](https://hmeyy.com/essays/visual-language.html): Bullet journals, bullets, checkboxes, mind maps, kanban boards and canvases. For an ADHD brain, marks and shapes do organizing work that words do badly, and short words beat sentences. So build a language for organization: a few signs, one meaning each, the same everywhere.
- [The Wall of Awful](https://hmeyy.com/essays/wall-of-awful.html): Brendan Mahan's name for the emotional pile-up behind a task: every bad attempt and every bit of guilt adds a brick, until the hard part is the feelings, not the task. Four ways to meet it, how to climb it in small kind steps, and how to keep it low.
- [What Each Religion Sells](https://hmeyy.com/essays/what-each-religion-sells.html): Every answer to the need can be read like a product: a problem, a promise, a technique, an exemplar and fine print. The major religions, read that way, and what each one suppresses.
- [What Is Enlightenment?](https://hmeyy.com/essays/what-is-enlightenment.html): What are you getting enlightened about? Not a subject. The original words mean waking up and blowing out. Kant’s enlightenment says stop buying your answers; the Buddha’s says see the one who needs them.
- [When This, Do That](https://hmeyy.com/essays/when-this-do-that.html): The art of planning ahead is moving every decision out of the moment I act and into a calm moment before it, ideally the night before. When this happens, I do that. Then the only question left is whether to start.
- [Why an Edge Feels Like Survival](https://hmeyy.com/essays/why-an-edge-feels-like-survival.html): Rank once decided survival, so the brain still treats an edge over others as life or death. What an edge really buys is control, it has no enough, and the urge underneath is security, significance or mastery.
- [The Why Behind the Need](https://hmeyy.com/essays/why-behind-the-need.html): Why all humans need to know what comes next, from the body up: the body pays for not knowing, the brain is built to remove it, the mind will take any answer, and culture answers the biggest one.
- [Why Belief Systems Survive](https://hmeyy.com/essays/why-belief-systems-survive.html): Hindu chants, kalasams and mudras have a clear internal logic. Most of it was written after the practice, and the whole system grew the way a reef does: no architect, shaped by what survived.
- [Always Work Backwards in a Plan](https://hmeyy.com/essays/work-backwards.html): Start at the finish line and walk back to something I can do today. The walk also shows what kind of problem I have: where it goes through cleanly, I don't need more strategy, just raw firepower. Only where it stalls do I need to think.
- [The goal is not a well-organized life](https://hmeyy.com/essays/work-not-organize.html): Organizing feels like work, and for a brain like mine it beats the real task every time. So it gets one place, set times, and nothing more.

## Projects

- [Condensr rebuild](https://hmeyy.com/projects/condensr.html): A visual thinking canvas, rebuilt in the browser from an open-source desktop tool I liked.
- [Game Dev](https://hmeyy.com/projects/game-dev.html): A pixel-art game built in Godot. Development log.
- [Voice agents](https://hmeyy.com/projects/live-voice-agent.html): Agents you talk to that do real work while you're talking: quotes, CRM updates, compliance questions.
- [Rain Café](https://hmeyy.com/projects/rain-cafe.html): A coffee shop in the rain, mixed live in your browser. Press the button at the bottom right.
- [Sleep Calculator](https://hmeyy.com/projects/sleep-calculator.html): Pick a wake-up time, get the bedtimes that land on a full sleep cycle.
- [Personal OS](https://hmeyy.com/projects/task-manager.html): The system I use to run my week, rebuilt more times than I'd like to admit.
